assumptions: The selected slice identifies unit 0 as paragraph 10 and units 3, 5 and 6 as paragraphs 14, 15 and 16.
Continuing responsibility can coexist with delegation of operational tasks.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.
6.8 The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.

6.8 The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders. The Commission must be advised on request of the address(es) where the register is kept.

6.11C Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party in ensuring such entity possesses the appropriate level of knowledge, experience and resources that commensurate with the appropriate valuation policies and procedures for each scheme. The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.

13. Where intermediaries issue (eg, fund managers of tokenised funds) or are substantially involved in the issuance of the Tokenised Securities which they intend to deal in or advise on, they remain responsible for the overall operation of the tokenisation arrangement notwithstanding any outsourcing to third-party vendors/service providers.

node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.distinction: This reading treats paragraph 10 primarily as allocating non-transferable accountability. A service failure need not prove that responsibility was transferred, although it may prove a separate performance failure. It does not treat contractual allocation alone as fulfillment of all operational requirements.
questions: What authority and practical ability to direct, obtain information from and remediate the outsourced arrangement must accompany retained accountability?
Does the applicable standard make particular supervisory conduct sufficient for the paragraph 10 control despite an operational failure?
node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.statement: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 can be read principally as retaining full and ultimate accountability with the Product Provider despite outsourcing. Governance and contractual allocation, backed by actual authority and conduct consistent with that allocation, could support a conclusion that responsibility was retained. They do not alone establish sound operations or proper ownership records. Section 6.8 permits specified actors to maintain the register and separately requires requested disclosure of its location; it does not displace the provider's responsibility. Section 6.11C expressly prescribes care in selection and monitoring for valuation outsourcing, but the packet does not make that standard the tokenisation fulfillment test.
node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.subject: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1: retained accountability as the selected control

assumptions: Responsibility for soundness and record keeping is read substantively alongside the express obligation to ensure proper records and compatibility.
An outcome-sensitive reading does not by itself establish strict liability for every incident.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.distinction: In the same case of active supervision but defective ownership records, retained authority would not justify declaring paragraph 10 fulfilled: the substantive subject of responsibility remains deficient. Conversely, accurate vendor records alone do not show that the provider retained responsibility. The rival readings differ over what paragraph 10 itself demands, not whether separate record-keeping duties matter.
questions: What severity, duration, remediation and assessment-period rules determine whether an operational or record defect defeats fulfillment?
node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.statement: Paragraph 10 can instead be read as requiring the Product Provider to secure the substantive soundness and ownership-record outcomes for which it remains fully responsible. A conclusion of fulfillment would require evidence connecting retained authority and exercised supervision to satisfactory operations and records under an applicable standard. No such standard or actual facts are supplied, so neither fulfillment nor a universal no-failure guarantee can be concluded.
node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.subject: Paragraph 10 as substantive responsibility for performance

node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.question: Has the Product Provider retained full ultimate accountability under paragraph 10 and footnote 1 despite delegated tasks? The candidate leaves uncertain whether supervisory discharge is also part of this selected fulfillment control.
node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.unit_of_assessment: Retention of responsibility by one Product Provider for one adopted tokenisation arrangement.
node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.temporal_basis: Continuously during the assessed arrangement, including outsourced performance; no specified assessment interval.
node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.true_means: Effective retained accountability is established through allocation backed by actual authority and consistent conduct, without certifying operations or records. Section 6.8 register maintenance and requested location disclosure remain separate; section 6.11C's valuation standard is not established as this control's test.
node.4053a6065a703c4e1349ce6a.false_means: Ultimate accountability has not been effectively retained. A service failure alone is insufficient to establish this; unresolved standards or facts do not themselves mean false.

node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.question: Has the Product Provider fulfilled paragraph 10's substantive responsibility by retaining authority, exercising supervision and securing satisfactory operational and ownership-record outcomes under the applicable standard?
node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.unit_of_assessment: One Product Provider's substantive responsibility for the operations and ownership records of one tokenisation arrangement.
node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.temporal_basis: During an assessment period not supplied by the excerpt; severity, duration and remediation rules remain unresolved.
node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.true_means: Retained responsibility and its satisfactory substantive discharge are established under this reading, considered with proper records and operational compatibility. Accurate vendor records alone or retained authority alone is insufficient. No universal no-failure guarantee is inferred.
node.93fd2924031e7f6efbde0a09.false_means: Substantive fulfillment fails under the applicable standard; neither every incident nor lack of evidence automatically establishes failure.
